translations.text: but he himself is the beginning, and he gave to all creatures a beginning and origin, so that they might exist, and so that they had their own nature, just as it pleased the divine ordering.
Now all these things are named with one name: creation. They were not always in existence, but God created them. The created things are many.
One is the Creator who created them all; he alone is Almighty God. He always was, and he will always be, continuing in himself and through himself.
but nevertheless, of the three there is one Godhead, and equal glory, and co-eternal majesty.
Truly the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit have one Godhead, and one nature, and one work.
The Father always was, and the Son always was, and the Holy Spirit always was, one Almighty God. He is the Father who is neither born nor created by any other.
The Holy Spirit is God proceeding from the Father and from the Son. These words are briefly said, and you need us to reveal them to you more clearly.
But I will give you an example, so that you may better understand God's begetting. Fire begets brightness from itself, and the brightness is just as old as the fire.
The fire is not from the brightness, but the brightness is from the fire. The fire begets the brightness, but it is never without the brightness.
Now you hear that the brightness is just as old as the fire from which it comes; grant now, therefore, that God could beget a Child just as old,
Now you have heard that the Son is from the Father without any beginning, because he is the Father's Wisdom, and he was always with the Father, and always will be.
The Holy Spirit is not a Son, because he is not begotten, but he proceeds from the Father and from the Son alike, because he is the Will and Love of them both.
The Father always was, without beginning; and the Son always was with the Father, because he is the Father's Wisdom; the Holy Spirit always was, who is the Will and Love of them both.
The sun that shines over us is a bodily creature, and yet it has three properties in it: one is the bodily substance, that is, the sun's disc;

the second is the beam or brightness that always comes from the sun, which lights the whole world; the third is the heat, which comes to us with the beam. The beam is always from the sun, and always with it;
None of them is greater than another, nor any less than another; none is before another, nor any after another;
Each of the three is God, yet they are all one God, because they all have one nature, and one Godhead, and one substance, and one counsel,
Yet the Holy Spirit is not Christ's Father, and no Christian must ever believe that; rather, the Holy Spirit is the Will of the Father and of the Son;
nevertheless, the heating belongs to the heat, and the illumination belongs to the brightness.
But know that no one can speak fully about God, since we cannot even examine or explain the creatures that he created.
Or who can [grasp] all other things, since we cannot even fully take in with our sight the bodily things that we look at?
Nothing is hidden or unknown to him. You see a person's face, and God sees his heart. The Spirit of God searches the hearts of all people;
Let everyone also know that every person has three things in himself, inseparable and working together, just as God said when he first created man.
A person's soul has in its nature the likeness of the Holy Trinity, because it has three things in it: memory, understanding, and will.
Yet none of these three is the soul itself. Rather, the soul remembers through the memory, understands through the understanding, and through the will it wills whatever pleases it;
Then the holy bishop Alexander said in reply to him, "God always was, and his Wisdom was always begotten of him, and that Wisdom is his Son, just as mighty as the Father."
When he came to the privy and sat down, all his entrails came out of him at the seat, and he sat there dead.
and again, when he wished, he would be the Holy Ghost; and so he would be one God. Then this heretic also perished along with his heresy.
Now again, the Jewish people, who killed Christ as he himself willed and allowed, say that they will believe in the Father, but not in the Son, whom their kinsmen killed.
We hold the faith that Christ himself taught his apostles, and that they taught to all mankind; and God has confirmed and established that faith with many miracles.
We must believe that every person's soul is created by God, yet it is not of God's own nature.
The soul does not exist anywhere beforehand. Instead, God creates it at that very moment and places it in the body, and lets it have its own free choice, whether to sin or to avoid sins.
Yet it always needs God's help so that it can avoid sins and come back to its Creator through good merits, because without God no one does anything good.
We must also believe that every body that has received a soul will rise on Judgement Day with the same body that it has now, and will receive the reward for all its deeds:
